description: find_header_boundary returns position + 4 (past CRLF-CRLF) or +2 (past LF-LF). The caller slices header_section = article_bytes[..body_start], meaning header_section includes the separator. This is functionally harmless (the loop skips blank lines) but the variable name 'header_section' is slightly misleading -- it actually contains header_section + separator. Naming it 'header_and_sep' or slicing with the pre-separator position would be clearer.
title: verify: find_header_boundary returns past-separator offset causing header_section to include separator bytes
